newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Paris Hard Rock Cafe complains to EU about closure.
newsitem.headline: Paris Hard Rock Cafe complains to EU about closure.

text.p: Hard Rock Cafe, part of an American-style chain owned by the Rank Organisation, said it complained to the European Commission on Tuesday that the closure of its Paris branch broke EU law.
French police closed the Hard Rock Cafe in Paris on November 6 after it found 300 kg (660 lbs) of frozen hamburger minced beef which it said was illegally imported from Britain.

The EU banned British beef in March in a bid to protect public health and restore consumer confidence after the British government said that mad cow disease could spread to people who ate infected beef.
But the Hard Rock Cafe says the minced meat came from Irish cattle, was processed into hamburgers in England at an EU-approved factory and legally exported.
"We have been politically ambushed," Peter Beaudrault, a senior Hard Rock vice president, said in a telephone interview.
"We have done nothing wrong. We are in full compliance with EU law."

Hard Rock's European operations director, Sally Woodward, said the company, which also has branches in six other EU states -- Spain, Denmark, Germany, Belgium, Sweden and Britain -- had met French conditions for reopening the Paris operation.
But French officials had made fresh demands and in a surprise visit on Tuesday had complained that the empty premises were dusty.
"It's now getting to harassment level," she said.

A Commission official confirmed that under a decision taken on June 11 non-British beef could be processed in Britain in authorised factories and re-exported subject to strict controls on the origin of the meat and production methods.
But the French police consider the Commission's decision is not binding on French territory.
If the Commission believes that the French police acted wrongly it could start proceedings against France on the grounds that it had infringed the EU treaty.
But some sources say this would be politically difficult given public concern about the health risk.
Hard Rock Cafe says the closure of its Paris branch has resulted in lost earnings of $650,000 and damaged its international reputation as a supplier of "safe, hygienic, high quality food products."
Hard Rock Cafe, founded in 1971 in Britain, is headquartered in Orlando, Florida, and has branches worldwide.
